items.stem: An AI tool generates 200 passing tests for a feature. Why is this not proof the feature is well tested?

options.text: The tests may miss important edge cases and critical paths
options.rationale: Correct: volume of passing tests does not equal meaningful coverage.

options.text: More tests always mean better coverage
options.rationale: Quantity does not guarantee the right coverage.

options.text: Passing tests prove there are no bugs
options.rationale: Passing tests only cover what they check.

items.explanation: Correct: volume of passing tests does not equal meaningful coverage.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep AI-assisted testing trustworthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Have a human review coverage of critical paths
options.rationale: Correct: human review ensures important paths are tested.

options.text: Verify AI-suggested root causes against evidence
options.rationale: Correct: verification prevents acting on wrong diagnoses.

options.text: Accept all AI tests without reading them
options.rationale: Blind acceptance risks weak or wrong tests.

options.text: Treat a green run as a guarantee of quality
options.rationale: A green run only reflects the tests that exist.

items.explanation: Correct: human review ensures important paths are tested.

items.stem: What is a key risk when using AI to generate test data from production examples?

options.text: Real personal or sensitive data could leak into test environments
options.rationale: Correct: using production-derived data can expose sensitive information.
Test data can contain or mirror sensitive information.

options.text: AI data is always perfectly representative
options.rationale: AI-generated data may be unrealistic or skewed.

options.text: Privacy rules never apply to testing
options.rationale: Privacy obligations extend to test data.

items.explanation: Correct: using production-derived data can expose sensitive information.
